reports.title: 3Q26 Earnings Release November 2026 Banking strength, technology at scale, a flywheel in motion

desk.headline: Record net income up 26% to R$425m on net revenue up 26% to R$2.72bn, in line with estimates; no numeric guidance
results: Net revenue rose 26% to R$2.72bn: net interest income grew 30% and fee income 13%.
Record net income of R$425m, up 26%; return on equity was 15.8%, up 1.6 points on a year ago but down from 16.3% in Q2.
The loan book grew 25% to R$58.1bn, led by private payroll loans (R$3.1bn, up 147%) and mortgages (up 37%); card lending growth was slowed to 18% on purpose.
Loans over 90 days late rose to 5.3%, but early arrears fell to 4.2% from 4.5%; cost of risk held at 5.9%.
Costs rose 17%, well below revenue, taking the efficiency ratio to 41.9%; deposits grew 19% to R$81bn.

guidance.summary: No numeric guidance was given. Management said it expects revenue to keep growing faster than costs and repeated its longer-term '60/30/30' ambition.

points: The CEO said bad loans are nearing their peak, helped by automatic re-linking of payroll loans when borrowers change jobs.
Card lending was deliberately slowed in a tough economy, favouring existing and higher-quality clients.
Management expects the gap between revenue and costs to keep widening, lifting efficiency and profits.
Heavy investment in automation: over 700 models run in production and the client assistant resolves about 85% of requests alone.
New leadership: Alexandre Riccio becomes COO and Francisco Santos joins as Chief Growth Officer; Santiago Stel stays CFO.
call.source: CEO letter in the 3Q26 earnings release (Exhibit 99.1); no independent call coverage found

watch: Whether over-90-day arrears peak as management expects, especially in private payroll and cards.
Net interest margin and funding cost if Brazil's Selic rate stays high.
